newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean plantings 72 percent done - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean plantings 72 percent done - Safras.

text.p: Brazilian soybean plantings were 72 percent completed by November 28 against 67 percent by November 30, 1995 and an average of the past five years of 70 percent, consultants Safras e Mercado said.
Plantings by November 21 this year were 52 percent.
The pace of plantings had picked up in the past week due to fewer rains generally throughout the growing regions, Safras said in its weekly report.

In some states planting slowed down from November 25 as farmers waited for more rainfall to return soil moisture levels to ideal conditions but this does not pose any real problems although good widespread rains would now be welcome.
Plantings of the 1996/97 crop by November 28 per state as estimated by Safras are as follows in percentage terms.

RIO GRANDE DO SUL - reasonable advances but widespread rains would now help. Credit problems could mean that not all the area hoped for will be planted PARANA - another active week keeping plantings well ahead of last year and the historical average. But lighter rainfall has meant there are some deficiencies in soil moisture, particularly in the Toledo (west) and Ivaipora (central) regions
MATO GROSSO DO SUL - plantings fell off as the week progressed in anticipation of fresh rainfall, particularly in the south GOIAS - favorable progress, especially between November 24-27

SAO PAULO - the lighter rains helped the speedy advance in sowings, especially in the Mogiana region from November 23 MINAS GERAIS - showed the best progress of all this week. After almost 10 days of rains, the weather improved and work in the field is now intense
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
